record.paper_title: Methods for Computing All Roots of a Polynomial Simultaneously - Known Results and Open Problems
record.context_brief: Additional nonconvergent starts for the Weierstrass method
record.original_question: Besides the already known critical starting vectors for which the Weierstrass algorithm fails, do there exist other initial approximation vectors for a polynomial's roots such that the full sequence of simultaneous approximations generated by the Weierstrass method does not converge?

evidence.quote: Are there other initial approximations, such that the sequence of approximations produced by the Weierstrass algorithm does not converge?
We can not answer the second question.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $p(z) = z^n + a_{n-1} z^{n-1} + \cdots + a_0 \in \mathbb{C}[z]$ be a monic polynomial of degree $n \geq 2$ with pairwise distinct roots. The Weierstrass (Durand–Kerner) iteration is the map $W_p \colon \mathbb{C}^n \to \mathbb{C}^n$ defined componentwise, for an approximation vector $z = (z_1,\dots,z_n)$ with pairwise distinct entries, by
$$ W_p(z)_i \;=\; z_i \;-\; \frac{p(z_i)}{\prod_{j \neq i} (z_i - z_j)}, \qquad i = 1, \dots, n. $$
Starting from an initial vector $z^{(0)} \in \mathbb{C}^n$, the iteration generates the sequence $z^{(k+1)} = W_p(z^{(k)})$. It is classically known that certain "critical" starting vectors (for instance, configurations whose entries are equally spaced on a circle centred at a root, or vectors mapped by $W_p$ outside its domain of definition) cause the iteration to fail to converge to the multiset of roots of $p$.

Question: Do there exist initial vectors $z^{(0)} \in \mathbb{C}^n$, beyond such already-identified critical starting configurations, for which the full sequence $\{z^{(k)}\}_{k \geq 0}$ produced by the Weierstrass iteration fails to converge to the root vector of $p$? Equivalently, is there a polynomial $p$ for which the set of non-converging initial vectors is strictly larger than the previously known exceptional set?
artifact.status_search_result: Recent work by Reinke, Schleicher and Stoll ("The Weierstrass root finder is not generally convergent", arXiv:2004.04777, 2020) and the subsequent paper on the Durand–Kerner version proves that for every degree $d \geq 3$ there are open sets of polynomials with open sets of initial vectors whose Weierstrass orbits converge to attracting periodic cycles different from the roots, and that almost every polynomial of degree $\geq 3$ admits orbits diverging to infinity. This affirmatively answers the question: there are non-converging starting vectors beyond the previously known critical ones, forming open sets of positive measure.

status_evidence.title: The Weierstrass root finder is not generally convergent
status_evidence.snippet: There are open sets of polynomials of every degree d ≥ 3 such that the dynamics of the Weierstrass method exhibits attracting periodic orbits; for almost every polynomial of degree d ≥ 3 there are orbits that converge to infinity.
status_evidence.claim: Open sets of starting vectors fail to converge for the Weierstrass iteration, beyond the previously known critical configurations.

status_evidence.title: The Weierstrass–Durand–Kerner root finder is not generally convergent
status_evidence.snippet: Several higher-dimensional methods for finding roots of univariate polynomials, in particular Weierstrass (Durand–Kerner), have infinite orbits that diverge to infinity, in both Jacobi and Gauss–Seidel update schemes.
status_evidence.claim: Diverging non-convergent orbits exist for the Durand–Kerner iteration, showing additional non-convergent starting vectors exist.
